newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mixed, Nov and Jan set new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mixed, Nov and Jan set new highs.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended mixed after soaring to new contract highs in nearbys on strength in cash lumber prices, traders said.

Futures ran up sharply on reports of cash lumber trading $415 per tbf versus Wednesday's $388 quote and posted new contract highs of $408.60 in November and $402.80 in January before slipping. November rallied a near limit of $9.90 early before closing up $6.30 at $405.00 per tbf. Other months ended off $3.10 to $4.50 with January off $3.10 at $397.30.
While higher cash kept November supported, deferred months were pressured by a bearish U.S. housing report, they said.
"That (report) is certainly bearish longer term but they have a little bit of a short-term supply squeeze going again here in November (contract)," one trader said.
Futures had started sharply lower following the release of the September housing report before November rallied on the cash advance, they said.

The Commerce Department reported a 6.0 percent drop in September housing starts to 1.438 million units from the previous month, the largest one month decline since January 1995's 9.0 percent drop. Building permits also declined 2.9 percent in September.
